questions.key_step: Two successive substitutions $\sqrt{\cos x}=t$ then $\sqrt{1+t^5}=u$.
questions.justification: Familiar substitution chain, but two stages and exact arithmetic with $\sqrt2$ and no options to check; precision risk lifts it above routine.

questions.key_step: King property twice ($x\to\pi-x$, then $x\to\pi/2-x$) before reaching a $\tan^{-1}$ integral.
questions.justification: Standard king property but needs it on two intervals plus a tan substitution; numerical format.

questions.key_step: Add $x\to-x$ copy to kill $1+e^{\sin x}$, then evaluate $\int dt/(1+t^4)$.
questions.justification: King-type trick is familiar; the $1/(1+t^4)$ evaluation with $\ln(3+2\sqrt2)$ is a known but lengthy second stage.

questions.key_step: Chain rule on $F(x^2)$ with $F'=xf$.
questions.justification: Routine multi-step Leibniz differentiation plus an AP sum; no insight beyond the rule.

questions.key_step: Split at points where $\cot x$ crosses integers.
questions.justification: Greatest-integer integral with monotone functions; routine casework, slip risk is moderate.

questions.key_step: Integration by parts whose leftover integral is $-18\alpha(11,5)$ (or spotting an exact derivative).
questions.justification: Needs recognising that the combination is a total derivative; short once seen but not a pattern most students expect.

questions.key_step: Compute $C_1,S_1,C_2,S_2,C_3$ in sequence.
questions.justification: Several routine polynomial integrations with fractions; long but no idea needed.

questions.key_step: Multiply and divide by $\sqrt{\sin x}$ to reveal a perfect derivative.
questions.justification: Hidden derivative structure in two big sums; unfamiliar idea, though the result $n^2$ is guessable from small $n$.

questions.key_step: Differentiate integral equation, then solve $y'-y/x=x^3$.
questions.justification: Routine two-stage chain: Leibniz then linear ODE then constant from $x=1$.

questions.key_step: Get $g=1/(1+x)$, then ODE collapses to $y'-y\tan x=2\sec x$.
questions.justification: Same chain as Q9 with trigonometric IF; routine.

questions.key_step: $3\tan^2x+3=3\sec^2x$ gives IF $e^{3\tan x}$.
questions.justification: Single familiar move: recognise the linear ODE and integrate.

questions.key_step: Write $e^{x-t}=e^xe^{-t}$ and differentiate to a linear ODE.
questions.justification: Integral equation to ODE to solution to area; routine chain of four standard steps.

questions.key_step: Multiply by $\sin y$, put $\cos y=t$, IF $x^7$, then integrate $x^2e^x$.
questions.justification: Non-obvious substitution and then by-parts; chain of three stages with options to check.

questions.key_step: Recognise IF $1+e^x/x^2$ (or exact $d(uy)$).
questions.justification: The integrating factor integral is not routine; spotting $\frac{d}{dx}(e^x/x^2)$ is the whole question.

questions.key_step: Quotient-rule form $\left(y/(1+x^2)\right)'$, then odd/even integral.
questions.justification: Two routine ideas chained; recognisable pattern.

questions.key_step: Compose $f,g$, IF $e^{2\sqrt x}$ cancels the exponential.
questions.justification: Routine chain with a neat cancellation.

questions.key_step: Treat $x$ as dependent variable; IF $e^{-1/y}$; by parts.
questions.justification: Routine once the variable is switched; by-parts adds a step.

questions.key_step: Set $y=0$ to turn the functional equation into $f'=f/2$.
questions.justification: Standard functional-equation trick then separable ODE and AP sum.

questions.key_step: Linear in $x$ with IF $e^{\tan^{-1}y}$.
questions.justification: Routine linear ODE in $dx/dy$ form with a nice substitution.

questions.key_step: $x\,dy-y\,dx=-y^2d(x/y)$ separates the variables.
questions.justification: Recognising the homogeneous combination is the key; sign care needed.
